newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crude slightly firmer at end month.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crude slightly firmer at end month.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices edged up Friday in line with broader market gains but trading was minimal due to end-of-month pipeline scheduling.
"Not only is there scheduling and people are finished for August but it is way too early to be thinking about September," said a refinery crude trader.
Regional benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, which last traded in the West Coast market in mid-June at $2.16 under benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, didn't trade on Friday.
August WTI was hardly changed on the day at $19.68/73, down a cent from the previous day, while September was up around 25 cents at $19.91/96.
Traders said dominant ANS seller BP Oil was still trying to get $1.85 under for the crude, but buyers were bidding $2.50 or more under, and there is plenty of alternative supply available.
"There are now four refiners running (Ecadorean) Oriente and by the end of August there will be five running (Mexican) Maya," said one trader.
Meanwhile, Arco Pipeline Co plans to announce its apportionment Monday for Line 63, the major pipeline between California's San Joaquin Valley (SJV) oil fields and Los Angeles refineries.
